title: Book One · Chapter 133: The Folded Corner
story:
The two weeks have ended. Miss Wu takes the street pictures down. Ronan holds the bottom of his cat drawing. One corner is folded, but the cat is still there behind its pot.

“Where will they go now?” Leo asks.

“Mei gets her pictures back. You get yours back,” she says. “We need the wall for our lessons now.”

She has a list of new words for the class. There are also numbers to put up. Ronan looks at the clean wall. He wants space for the lessons and the pictures. There is not enough room for both.

He lays the pictures on two desks. The map goes under a board. He puts Mum's picture between two sheets. The paper will keep it clean. Mr Qiu's table drawing is the largest. It is too big for his bag. He wants to keep it flat.

“Leave it here tonight,” Miss Wu says. “Take it home flat tomorrow.”

Ronan looks at the window. Rain has stopped, but clouds are coming over the roof again. He puts the drawing on a high, dry shelf. It is away from the glass.

At home he tells Mum the wall is empty. She is sewing a small square of cloth inside her blue bag. She has chosen a mark for her bags. It is a little open square with two lines below. It looks like a pocket.

“I can put your picture above our table,” he says.

“We can look for a place.”

“And Mr Qiu's?”

“Ask him. He can choose a place for it.”

Mr Qiu is counting notebooks at the little table. He hears the question and takes off his glasses.

“How many drawings do you have?”

Ronan counts on his fingers. There is Mr Qiu's table and the cat. There is Mum testing the bag with stones. There is the map he made with Leo. Mei has her own pictures too.

“You need somewhere to keep them flat,” Mr Qiu says.

He has two clean boards from an old paper box. He can put the drawings between the two boards. He can tie the boards together. He offers to show Ronan. The boards are not a gift yet. Mr Qiu still needs them for a few days.

“After I put my new paper away, you may have them.”

“Will the pictures stay good?”

“Better than in a ball under your bed.”

Ronan smiles. There is no ball of paper there now. There was one last week.

The next day he carries the drawing home flat. Mum walks beside him. They stop twice so other people can pass. At the green gate the wind catches one end. Ronan holds the drawing with both hands. Mum opens the gate all the way for him.

Nothing tears. Inside, Mr Qiu clears his table and lets them lay the drawing down. He looks at the small drawn sign with his name.

“I think I would like this one in the side space,” he says. “Above the boxes. If Mrs Lan agrees.”

Mrs Lan comes to look. She says it can go on the inside of the little door, away from the rain. Ronan holds it there while she finds two small clips.

Mr Qiu asks him to open the door halfway. From the yard the drawing is hidden. From the shelf he can see it clearly. He wants the picture inside this little door. Ronan takes his hands away. He checks both clips. They do not catch on the wood. The drawing stays flat when the door moves.

The picture was on the classroom wall before. Now Mr Qiu has a place for it here. Ronan opens and closes the door gently. The picture stays safely on the inside.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：flat＝平放、平整；clips＝夹子；inside＝在里面。

情节提示：pocket＝口袋；tie＝用绳绑；glasses＝眼镜。

理解：1. 为什么课堂上的画必须取下？2. Mr Qiu 最后把自己的画放在哪里？
